order.why_here: The base case: a closed window [lo, hi] that traps the target and halves on every comparison.
Drops the equality check and searches for a border, the first F of nums[i] < target, which may be n.
Two borders from one half-open lower-bound helper: lower(t) and lower(t+1) - 1.
The candidates become virtual positions; divmod folds a flat index back into the grid.
Sortedness breaks into two runs; the predicate compares mid with the right end, not with a target.
Searches a target in the same rotated array by testing whichever half is a clean sorted ramp.
The predicate becomes a slope sign that is only locally monotone; a T at the left edge and F at the right edge suffice.
Composes a summit search and two slope searches under a 100-read budget; search order picks the smaller index.
First binary search on the answer: candidates are speeds and P is a greedy hours count.
Maximize the minimum gap: the answer is the last T, checked by greedy placement.
Minimize the maximum piece sum: the same answer search with a greedy piece-count check.
The feasibility check becomes a capped sum instead of a simulation.
Binary search on a value and count entries at most the guess to find the k-th smallest.
Same k-th-by-counting idea, with the count done by two pointers over a sorted array.
A real-valued answer: subtract the guess and test a prefix-sum condition, iterate to precision.
The candidates are cut positions in the shorter array; P compares values across the cut.
